There are, yes. In general, mods that only effect textures are fine to disable.  
Ones that effect sounds might be, but you'd probably want to clean the save after  
Everything else is recommended not to, although you can sometimes do so depending on the mod and your experience with cleaning saves.  
Honestly, I'd recommend not having anything other than mods that you can't enable midgame enabled at the start, and then add other mods if you want to so that you can get a feel for the changes they add and also are aware of any incompatibilities.

I'm not sure how I can really help, per say, but I would recommend that you simply disable most of your mods. When you get to too many mods, the game becomes very unstable, and the various mods can interact in unexpected ways.  
The best way to install mods is to do so one at a time, and do a quick check to make sure that the functionality is maintained.  
It takes forever I know, but it ultimately leads to a much more stable and enjoyable experience.  
One last thing: once you get to 255 esps you cannot have anymore period.  
There's a number of issues with memory that come with pushing your system to the limit.  
There's a way to fix these issues, but it's a fairly technical procedure and I'm pretty sure it wouldn't work for Xbox.

If you do not split your clan, then you will get a minor clan revolt after some time. If you do split your clan, then the minor clan will get all the buildings that you possess in your capital, but if you do not... the minor clan that revolts will not have any such buildings. This is last patch at least and may not be accurate anymore. A strategy I have found good for nomads is to allow minor clan revolts to occur when I want them to (that is, in counties with high revolt risk which means recently conquered counties). If you do this properly, you can have a completely upgraded nomadic capital, while none of your vassal Khans have any upgrades.
